why: For t = 5 nothing is printed. The outer if (t > 10) is false, and because the else belongs to the inner if (the dangling-else rule), no 'cold' is printed. All three tests in the else-if chain are also false. The student gets the right result and explains it by tying the else to the nested if structure, but does not mention the second chain.

concepts.quote: the outer if fails and the else is part of the inner if
concepts.why: Correctly uses the dangling-else rule: without braces the else pairs with the inner if, so a false outer test skips both branches.

concepts.quote: the else is part of the inner if
concepts.why: Correctly sees that the if-else is the branch of an outer if, so its else is never reached here.
